hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes Adam into divergence.
At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained in 243 epochs, so a larger step helps a lot.
Lowering a divergent learning rate recovers accuracy, whereas lowering a moderate one gives little or harms.
Large batches have less gradient noise and fewer updates, so they tolerate and benefit from bigger steps.
With a tiny learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and worse undertraining.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at aggressive learning rates.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty causes severe underfitting, while increases at small alpha are negligible.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units at large learning rates.
Strong weight decay compounded over more layers shrinks the signal and worsens underfitting.
Adding units helps most when capacity is the bottleneck and has diminishing returns at large widths.
